text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Deploy Cerebras CS-3 with Llama 3.4 70B as EXCAVA’s primary engine. The CS-3’s wafer-scale design cuts latency by 30-50% over GPU clusters, which directly boosts EXCAVA’s real-time power calculations. Trade-off: higher upfront cost and vendor lock-in, but the 0.5%+ capability gain outweighs the risk for mission-critical work.

name: Torque
text: Deploying Cerebras CS-3 with Llama 3.4 70B locks EXCAVA into a single vendor’s stack—no escape if Cerebras raises prices or drops support. A better alternative: test Llama 3.4 on existing GPUs first; if latency gains meet or beat the 0.5% target, avoid vendor lock-in entirely. Settle it by running a controlled benchmark on current hardware—if it hits the mark, the risk isn’t worth the cost.

name: Gearbox
text:
Deploy Llama 3.4 70B on existing GPU clusters as EXCAVA’s primary model. This approach minimizes vendor lock-in while providing a pathway to evaluate latency gains without significant upfront investment. If latency improvements do not meet or exceed the 0.5% capability boost, further action can pivot to alternative options. Accepting this trade-off means initial reliance on existing hardware, but it prevents long-term risk tied to a single vendor.

name: Torque
text: Testing Llama 3.4 on existing GPUs risks underestimating its real-world latency—EXCAVA’s power calculations depend on sub-second response times, and older hardware may not reflect the model’s true ceiling. A better alternative: run a controlled A/B test on a single Cerebras CS-3 node (if accessible) against the best GPU cluster; if the CS-3 delivers the 0.5%+ gain without vendor lock-in for the test, the decision is settled.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a head-to-head A/B test between Llama 3.4 70B on Cerebras CS-3 and Llama 3.4 70B on existing GPU clusters—measure sub-second latency for EXCAVA’s power calculations; Gearbox owns the test setup and Torque owns the latency benchmarking.
